title: Make Costs of Paths Equal in a Binary Tree
summary: Given a perfect binary tree with n nodes, where each node i has a cost represented by an array cost, determine the minimum number of increments needed to make the cost of paths from the root to each leaf node equal.
statement: Given a perfect binary tree with n nodes, where each node i has a cost represented by an array cost, determine the minimum number of increments needed to make the cost of paths from the root to each leaf node equal. Each node can have its cost incremented by 1 any number of times. A perfect binary tree has each non-leaf node with exactly two children, and the cost of a path is the sum of the costs of the nodes in that path.
constraints: Nodes one through n form a perfect binary tree in heap order and cost[i-1] is node i’s positive cost.
You may increment any node cost by one per operation.
Return the minimum operations making every root-to-leaf path sum equal.
hints: Process internal nodes from the deepest level upward.
Sibling subtrees must end with equal path cost, so raise the cheaper side by their absolute difference.
Add the larger balanced child path cost into the parent before continuing upward.
Each sibling imbalance must be paid somewhere exclusively in its cheaper subtree; paying it immediately is sufficient and leaves the exact common cost needed by the parent.

tests.explanation: Balancing sibling subtrees bottom-up requires six total increments.
Both root-to-leaf paths already cost eight, so no increment is needed.
